# dss rules digest (one line per rule)

Detailed rules load automatically for the files you touch (`.claude/rules/`).
On-demand rules: read `.claude/rules-ondemand/<name>.md` when the topic comes up.

- **dss-a11y**: WCAG 2.2 AA: semantic HTML, visible focus, labelled controls, real alt text, contrast guaranteed by DNA tokens.
- **dss-actions**: Every public mutation goes through safeAction (zod, honeypot, per-IP rate limit, Turnstile) and returns ActionResult.
- **dss-ai-files**: dss-* files in .claude/ are overwritten by the sync from core/_ai; site-specific ones are prefixed site-.
- **dss-client**: "use client" only in small leaf components that need state, effects or browser APIs; pass server data down as props.
- **dss-content**: All visible text lives here, typed `as const`; replace every [placeholder] with specific, verifiable facts.
- **dss-data**: Drizzle only in server/; schema in server/db/schema.ts, migrations generated and committed; every file imports 'server-only'.
- **dss-images**: Media (next/image) with a real alt, a ratio and sizes; priority only on the LCP image; no placeholder left at launch.
- **dss-manifest**: site.manifest.ts and design.dna.ts are data files rewritten by the CLI: literal values only, validated at import.
- **dss-motion**: Motion follows the DNA profile (none, subtle, expressive, cinematic); animate transform/opacity only; honour reduced motion.
- **dss-naming**: PascalCase components, useX hooks, kebab-case files and routes, files <= 250 lines, no `any`, `@/` imports.
- **dss-routes**: Pages are thin server components: pageMetadata + sections fed from content/; no copy, no logic, no "use client".
- **dss-sections**: Sections are owned code: typed props from content/, @dss/ui primitives, DNA tokens; first line stamp, then a @catalog JSDoc.
- **dss-seo**: Metadata, canonical, robots, sitemap, llms.txt and JSON-LD come from @dss/seo and the manifest; previews are noindexed automatically.
- **dss-styles**: Only DNA token classes: no hex/rgb, no arbitrary colors, no default Tailwind palette (bg-slate-900, text-indigo-500), no inline style.
- **dss-three**: three/@react-three only in components/3d, client-only, lazy, rendered through <Scene> with a poster fallback; never the LCP.
- **dss-cms** (on demand): Default: content/ files edited through Claude or Git; client editing via the cms-keystatic module (Git-based, free).
- **dss-copywriting** (on demand): Voice from site.spec.md; specific, verifiable, plain; one idea per sentence; no generated-copy tells.
- **dss-core-dev** (on demand): Change the framework in the daroms-speed-site repository (never in a site's core/); test, then release.
- **dss-csp-nonce** (on demand): Only when a third party requires strict-dynamic: it forces dynamic rendering of every page and is incompatible with cacheComponents.
- **dss-database-advanced** (on demand): D1 for Cloudflare sites, libSQL/Turso for Docker, Postgres (Neon) when relational load or extensions require it.
- **dss-deploy-cloudflare** (on demand): OpenNext on Workers: `pnpm cf:preview` locally, `DSS_ENV=preview pnpm cf:deploy` for a preview, `pnpm cf:deploy` for production.
- **dss-deploy-docker** (on demand): `deploy.target: 'docker'` builds standalone output; `pnpm docker:build` then run behind a TLS proxy (Coolify, Dokploy, Caddy).
- **dss-deploy-vercel** (on demand): Set `deploy.target: 'vercel'`; `pnpm exec vercel` for previews (noindexed via VERCEL_ENV), `pnpm exec vercel --prod` for production.
- **dss-legal-gdpr** (on demand): A legal notice and a privacy page before launch; cookieless analytics by default so no consent banner is needed.
- **dss-performance-budget** (on demand): LCP < 2.0s, CLS < 0.05, INP < 200ms on mobile; Lighthouse >= 90 performance and >= 95 accessibility, best practices, SEO.
